page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with Greek and Latin inline; italic quotations and indented verse; marginal notes in the left margin; catchword at lower right.

main_text.p: t. Aug.[?]ritu reperio. Tacitus de seditiosis: Congerunt cespites, ex-struunt Tribunal. Lucanus de Cæsare:

p.i: Lib.v.— stetit aggere fulti Cespitis intrepidus vultu.
Hic suetus dare iura pater, hoc cespite turmas Affari.[?]

main_text.p: In Nero- ne.Dio, de Boundica regina Britanniæ: ἡ ἀνίςη[?] ἐπὶ τὸ ἔθνμα[?] ἐκ γῆς ἑλώδους ἐς τὸν ῥωμαϊκὸν τέγπον[?] πεποιημένον: Et conscendit tribunal è terra palustri, Romanum in morem fa-ctum. Mulier scilicet illa plus cordis habuit, quàm multi viri: & militem suum non duxit solùm, sed publicè affata est & instruxit. idque Romano ritu, in cespite, ut Milites ordinati in audiendo.Dio notat. Circa autem hunc cespitem sive tribunal, milites dispositi non confusè nec ut quisque accurrerat, t. Ann.[?]sed per manipulos & turmas. Germanicus Cæsar apud Tacitum, Concionem, quia permissa videbatur, discedere in manipulos iubet; vexilla præferri, ut id saltem discerneret cohortes. Ubi & vexilla prælata notes, id est Signa manipulorum turmarumque & ipsarum legionum. Plinius in Laudatione Traiani: Multa post sæcula tribunal viridi cespite exstructum, nec fascium tantùm sed *Necmale horrere.pilorum signorumque {*}honore circumdatum. Laudat in Traiano, quod is quoque ritu prisco militem affatus sit: ritu, qui exoleuerat sub Domitiano & eiusmodi ignavis. Affatus autem, inquit, in cespite: quem non cum fascibus lictores solùm adstarent, sed circumstarent milites cum Pilis & Signis. Ergo armati: & sic Claudianus:

p.i: De bell. Gnidon.Dictis ante tamen Princeps confirmat ituros, Aggere conspicuus. stat circumfusa iuventus Nixa hastis, pronâsque ferox accommodat aures.

page.notes: Marginal notes at the top left ("t. Aug.", "t. Ann.") are hard to read and may be "1." with a lowercase form; marked [?]. "In Nero- ne." is split over two lines; the second part is read as "ne.". The Greek of the Dio passage is read from a difficult scan: the first word, the word after "ἔθνμα", and "τέγπον" are doubtful and marked [?]; the Greek should be checked against the printed edition. "Affari" is doubtful and marked [?]. The star "*" after "signorumque" is a printed reference mark, matched by the note "*Necmale horrere.". The "Lib.v." note is set in the verse paragraph because it stands beside those lines.
